## What this note should cover

- **Why cross-section averages work as factor proxies**: averaging the
  observed variables recovers the space spanned by the unobserved factors, so
  the factors need never be estimated.
- **Heterogeneous loadings** as the case two-way fixed effects cannot absorb —
  the identity carried over from
  [cross-sectional dependence](theory-cross-sectional-dependence.qmd).
- **CCEMG vs CCEP**: averaging unit-by-unit slopes against pooling them, and
  what each assumes about slope homogeneity.
- How to read the two together: close estimates support the pooling
  restriction, as the MG-to-CCEMG jump from 0.30 to 1.14 in the example shows.
- What CCE does **not** fix, and when interactive fixed effects are the better
  answer.
